note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Washburn RD): loops in red and white pine and hardwoods between Lake Owen and Bass Lake, many sites looking at a lake through the trees. Two swim beaches, a boat launch on each lake and a fishing pier on Bass Lake; the North Country Trail passes through the campground. ATVs and UTVs are barred in the campground. --Claude
summary: FS page + rec.gov read: 94 sites (7 walk-in tent), $25, vault toilets, water, dump ($10), 50-ft max vehicle, pull-throughs, 14-night max, 4-day cutoff, 55 reservable/39 FCFS; season May 1-Oct 31 (manual) matches. Lakeview kept (canopy). Count 67 -> 94. Pin ~800 m off at the entrance.
flags: WATERFRONT: lakeview kept. The shore loops are under continuous canopy on Esri imagery: sites 006-011 on the Lake Owen shore (e.g. 007 at 46.29529,-91.19052, 010 at 46.29473,-91.19175) sit ~25-40 m back through trees; sites 066-075 on the south bay (068 at 46.29196,-91.19143 ~15-20 m, 072 at 46.29222,-91.19089 ~30 m) and 078-084 on the east bay likewise. rec.gov photos of 068 and 072 show the lake beyond a stand of trunks. The FS says 'many overlook' the lakes and rec.gov 'most sites offer sweeping lake views' - consistent with lakeview, not lakefront.

PIN MOVE (>250 m): stored 46.2972,-91.1856 is at the entrance/fee station area east of the campground (the FS page gives 46.29583,-91.1875). The 94 site coordinates centre at 46.2932,-91.1945; place the pin on the central loop at ~46.2935,-91.1940 (~780 m from the stored point).

FEES: the FS page contradicts itself - 'Single Site: $25 per night' and 'Individual campsite fee is $23, or $11.50 with the use of an Interagency pass'. rec.gov's 2026-2028 rate table says $25, written.

SITES: count 67 (derived) -> 94 per FS and rec.gov; max_rig_ft 50 from the rec.gov notice ('Maximum vehicle size is 50 feet'); the FS 'Corrals: RV up to 50 Feet' agrees. rec.gov per-site lengths (e.g. 15 ft at 8, 9, 64, 81, 87) disagree with the FS's 30-35 ft lists; most sites fit a 23-ft rig either way.

INCLUSION_EVIDENCE: stored text says '94 Standard Nonelectric drive-in sites'; 7 are walk-in tent sites.
